bienvenida.title: How to walk it
bienvenida.body: This site is a path. As you scroll you move along it, and each place in Kyoto appears when you reach it. To jump to another section, use the stone rail on the right (on a phone, the bar at the bottom). 音 turns on the ambient sound and 静 quiets the scene.

capital.title: The thousand-year capital
capital.body: In 794 Emperor Kanmu moved the court to this valley and named it Heian-kyō, “the capital of peace and tranquility”. For more than a thousand years, until 1868, it was the heart of the country: the emperors lived here, and from here the roads set out to every province.

heian.title: A city laid out with a cord
heian.body: Heian-kyō (as Kyoto was called back then) was laid out in the image of Chang’an, the Tang capital: a grid of about 4.5 by 5.2 km, with the palace to the north and Suzaku Avenue, some 85 metres wide, running down to the Rashōmon gate. Today’s streets still carry its numbers: Nijō, Shijō, Gojō.

kyoto.title: From Heian-kyō to Kyoto
kyoto.body: Over the centuries the city came to be called simply Kyoto, 京都, “the capital”. In 1868 the emperor moved to Tokyo, but the city kept what it had gathered: more than 1,600 temples, some 400 shrines and seventeen World Heritage monuments. The ancient and the everyday still share the same street.
